questiontext.text: Explain the process of encapsulation in the TCP/IP model.

generalfeedback.text:
Expected Model Answer

Encapsulation is the process of wrapping data with protocol headers as it travels down the TCP/IP stack.

  • Application Layer: User data is generated.
  • Transport Layer: A TCP or UDP header is added, creating a segment.
  • Internet Layer: An IP header is added, creating a packet.
  • Network Access Layer: An Ethernet header and trailer are added, creating a frame.
  • The frame is converted into bits and transmitted over the physical medium.

Key points for full marks:

  • Defines encapsulation correctly.
  • Mentions all TCP/IP layers in the correct order.
  • Explains the addition of protocol headers.
  • Correctly identifies segment, packet, and frame.

questiontext.text: Why is TCP considered reliable while UDP is not? Give one use case for each.

generalfeedback.text:
Expected Model Answer

TCP is reliable because it is connection-oriented and uses:

  • Sequencing
  • Acknowledgments (ACKs)
  • Retransmission of lost packets
  • Error detection

TCP is commonly used for applications that require accurate and complete delivery, such as:

  • HTTP/HTTPS (web browsing)
  • SMTP (email)

UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery, ordering, or retransmission, making it faster but less reliable.

Typical UDP applications include:

  • Video/audio streaming
  • DNS queries

Key points for full marks:

  • Explains why TCP is reliable.
  • Explains why UDP is unreliable.
  • Provides one correct TCP use case.
  • Provides one correct UDP use case.

questiontext.text:
State the OSI layer for each of the following and give one security or forensic relevance:

  1. IP
  2. DNS
  3. Ethernet

generalfeedback.text:
Expected Model Answer

Protocol OSI Layer Security / Forensic Relevance
IP Network Layer (Layer 3) IP spoofing attacks occur at this layer. Investigators analyze IP headers to trace communication sources.
DNS Application Layer (Layer 7) DNS poisoning and DNS tunneling attacks. DNS logs can reveal Command-and-Control (C2) communication during forensic investigations.
Ethernet Data Link Layer (Layer 2) MAC spoofing and ARP poisoning attacks. Ethernet frames help identify devices on a local network during investigations.

Key points for full marks:

  • Correctly identifies the OSI layer for all three protocols.
  • Provides an appropriate security or forensic relevance for each protocol.
